gloss: intermittence; on and off; starting and stopping

definitions.gloss: intermittence; on and off; starting and stopping
definitions.explanation: The pattern of repeatedly stopping and starting, or occurring at intervals rather than continuously. Almost always used in the adverbial form {断続的|だんぞくてき}に.

examples.japanese: {断続的|だんぞくてき}に{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}っている。
{断続的|だんぞくてき}な{頭痛|ずつう}に{悩|なや}まされている。
{交渉|こうしょう}は{断続的|だんぞくてき}に{行|おこな}われ、{最終的|さいしゅうてき}に{合意|ごうい}に{達|たっ}した。
examples.english: Negotiations were held intermittently, and ultimately an agreement was reached.

notes:
A compound of {断|だん} (to cut off, interrupt) and {続|ぞく} (to continue). The word combines two opposing concepts — interruption and continuation — to describe a pattern of repeated stopping and starting.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {断続的|だんぞくてき}に: intermittently, on and off
- {断続的|だんぞくてき}な{雨|あめ}: intermittent rain
- {断続的|だんぞくてき}な{痛|いた}み: intermittent pain
- {断続的|だんぞくてき}な{渋滞|じゅうたい}: stop-and-go traffic

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {間欠的|かんけつてき}: intermittent — more technical/scientific; used for geysers, fevers
- {連続|れんぞく}: continuous, consecutive — the antonym, meaning without interruption
- {継続|けいぞく}: continuation — sustained over time without the stopping-and-starting nuance

USAGE:
Most commonly appears as {断続的|だんぞくてき} (adjective) or {断続的|だんぞくてき}に (adverb). Very frequently used in weather forecasts ({断続的|だんぞくてき}な{雨|あめ}) and news reports.
